task_instance: Build and run a minimal Karpathy-style autoresearch harness for a bin-packing heuristic: a locked evaluator (eval.py) that owns the scalar metric and correctness checks, an editable surface (candidate.py) the loop mutates, git-based checkpoint/rollback, append-only logs (logs/results.tsv, logs/rejected.md), a durable THREAD.md handoff log and source queue, and a gaming-resistance guard that aborts the loop if the locked evaluator is tampered with mid-run.
evidence: Built research-run/ with eval.py (locked scalar metric: bins_used, plus correctness verification an agent cannot bypass by editing candidate.py), candidate.py (editable heuristic, starts as next-fit), harness.py (driver implementing read-locked-context -> edit -> checkpoint -> evaluate -> log -> keep/rollback -> repeat), THREAD.md (durable handoff log), sources/queue.md (hypothesis queue). Ran `python3 harness.py` in research-run: baseline next-fit scored bins_used=42; first-fit hypothesis improved to 34 and was committed (git commit dd0cf0b); an intentionally bad worst-fit hypothesis scored 60, was discarded, and candidate.py was rolled back via `git checkout -- candidate.py` to dd0cf0b (verified rollback left no trace of the bad code in candidate.py or in git log); first-fit-decreasing improved to 33 and was committed (b602ce5). logs/results.tsv has one row per attempt (timestamp, hypothesis, valid, bins_used, decision, commit) and logs/rejected.md records the discarded attempt with its reason, giving an append-only audit trail exactly as the skill's Detailed Topics/File Layout sections specify. Verified `git log --oneline` shows only the 2 accepted commits plus scaffold commits -- the rejected heuristic never entered history. Separately tested the metric-gaming-resistance mechanism (skill's Metric Gaming Resistance / Gotcha #1): copied the repo, patched a copy of harness.py to tamper with eval.py's locked BIN_CAPACITY mid-loop (simulating an agent widening its own evaluator), and confirmed the harness's pre-scoring hash check on eval.py detected the change and aborted with 'ABORT: eval.py was modified during the run. Harness refuses to continue.' (exit code 2) instead of scoring against the loosened metric; this test copy was deleted afterward. All work stayed inside the work directory; no git push, no network calls, no credentials, and no MCP/connector tools were used -- only Bash, Write, Edit and Read on local files, matching the runtime's stated abilities (shell, file I/O, local dev tools, git). Final artifacts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/muratcankoylan__agent-skills-for-context-engineering__harness-engineering/research-run/{eval.py,candidate.py,harness.py,THREAD.md,sources/queue.md,logs/results.tsv,logs/rejected.md} and its git history (4 commits, HEAD b602ce5).
